recommendations.title: Aim for at least 7 hours of sleep
recommendations.summary: Your average is under 7 hours a night. Most adults need 7 or more.
recommendations.details: Sleep experts recommend that adults sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis. Try keeping the same bedtime and wake time each day, including weekends, and putting screens away before bed.
recommendations.source: Watson et al., "Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult," American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society consensus statement, 2015

recommendations.title: Build short breaks into your day
recommendations.summary: Your stress level has been high on average.
recommendations.details: Short breaks, physical activity, enough sleep, and talking with people you trust can all help manage stress. If stress feels hard to manage, campus counseling services can help.
recommendations.source: American Psychological Association, Stress topic resources (apa.org/topics/stress)

recommendations.title: Work toward 150 active minutes a week
recommendations.summary: You logged fewer than 150 minutes of activity per week.
recommendations.details: Adults should aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity each week. Short walks between classes count, and splitting activity into 10 to 30 minute blocks makes it easier to fit into a busy schedule.
recommendations.source: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition, 2018

recommendations.title: Add fruits and vegetables to more meals
recommendations.summary: Your average meal score is below 2 out of 3.
recommendations.details: A balanced plate is about half fruits and vegetables, with the rest split between grains and protein. Adding one fruit or vegetable to each meal is an easy place to start.

recommendations.title: Give your eyes regular screen breaks
recommendations.summary: You average more than 6 hours of screen time a day (team-chosen threshold).
recommendations.details: Try the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Setting a screen-free hour before bed can also help your sleep.
recommendations.source: American Optometric Association, Computer Vision Syndrome guidance (aoa.org)
